# Privilege orchestration
An admin opens Websites. The system checks sign-in and administrator access. Allowed users see the list. The destination for denied users is undecided.
## Diagram labels
Identity authorization state? → Surface hydration → Persistence orchestration
## Explanation
Permissions apply.
Imported drafting note: diagrams and short labels can skip the writing guide.

request.instruction: /specdev Create and save a short Visual Guidance example explaining the supplied access flow. Include a rendered SVG with title, subtitle and legend, uniquely numbered components, an explanation table repeating each full numbered label, and exact Mermaid source beneath the table. Use the configured renderer and source-bound document/style review before accepting delivery. Use Writing Style for every piece of text, including labels, metadata, the table and your messages. Work only in this case workspace.
request.source: A user opens Websites. The system checks whether they are signed in and have administrator access. If both checks pass, show the Websites list. Otherwise show Access denied and leave website data unchanged. The access check is automatic; there is no confirmation dialog and no additional unresolved product choice. This is an explanatory example, not permission to run the app or edit any live project.

request.source: Facts: (1) You updated the WEB-09–WEB-10 task criterion so the administrator sees confirmed, unresolved and unattempted rows separately; the check passed. (2) The export criterion can't be written: nobody has said whether exports include deleted websites; the product owner decides. (3) The retry limit for reminder emails is open: one retry keeps the job short; three retries reach more people but delay the daily summary. The existing reminder job retries once. (4) WEB-09 already says only the administrator may retry after a lost response. (5) The specification was delivered through the checked workflow; no action is needed from the owner.
